14913293.reason: Evenness is insufficient: n=6 never visits all six positions; only powers of two give complete coverage. Pure bounded integer decision, no presentation or resource artifacts; explicit periodic visited-set proof refutes the even-n rule.

counterexample.constraints: One integer n in 1..1000. Independently parsed successfully; LF audit copy only, package bytes unchanged.
counterexample.mathematicalDerivation: At jump k the position is T_k=k*(k+1)/2 mod 6, translating the starting hassock to 0. Independent finite-state simulation of (position,next jump mod n) returns to an already seen state after 12 states, hence exhausts the infinite orbit. Its visited set is [0, 1, 3, 4], of size 4 versus n=6. Therefore the required answer is NO.

import math

n = int(sys.stdin.readline())

v = [0] * n
ost = 1
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    ost = (ost + i) % n
    v[ost] = 1

for i in v:
    if(i == 0):
        print("NO")
        exit()
    
print("YES")
